Article.ArticleTitle: Modest loss of sleep increases susceptibility to cybersecurity threats.

Abstract.AbstractText: Sleep restriction leads to impaired cognitive processing across domains. I examined whether the transition to daylight saving time (DST), typically accompanied by compromised sleep, would lead to an increase in the probability of falling prey to a simulated phishing attack using a fully naturalistic experiment with random assignment and blinding. A predatory email was sent to employees at the University of California, Irvine (N = 11,218) either on the morning of Monday following the transition to DST or one week earlier. The transition led to a ~13% increase in the probability of clicking a suspicious link, without affecting the probability of opening the email or reporting it as spam. These results demonstrate that even modest, mundane, and acute loss of sleep has real-life, potentially hazardous, implications for cognitive function.

Article.ArticleTitle: Impact of combined chronic stress and REM sleep deprivation on memory function and hippocampal BDNF protein content in Wistar rats.

Abstract.AbstractText: The concurrent impact of chronic psychological stress and sleep disruption on systemic adaptation and hippocampal cytoarchitecture remains poorly understood. This study investigated the neurobiological threshold of compounded stress by exposing male Wistar rats to combined Chronic Unpredictable Mild Stress (CUMS) and Rapid Eye Movement Sleep Deprivation (RSD), specifically chosen over total sleep deprivation due to the unique role of REM sleep in emotional regulation and spatial memory consolidation over 21 days. We evaluated body weight loss, sensorimotor function Open Field Test (OFT), declarative memory Novel Object Recognition (NOR), serum corticosterone, hippocampal malondialdehyde (MDA), and Brain-Derived Neurotrophic Factor (BDNF). Results revealed that the combined stress paradigm precipitated significant body weight loss while preserving basal locomotor activity. In contrast to motor preservation, spatial recognition memory was significantly impaired. Biochemically, serum corticosterone and hippocampal MDA levels did not show statistically significant differences across groups. Crucially, while isolated CUMS significantly suppressed hippocampal BDNF protein content and RSD exhibited a similar trend of reduction, the combined paradigm triggered a compensatory neurotrophic rebound, returning BDNF to control baseline levels. However, the localized BDNF rebound did not translate to recovery cognitive performance. These findings suggest a phenomenon of neurobiological dissociation under compounded stress exposure. The organism experiences significant body weight loss and declarative memory impairment, while simultaneously initiating a localized, yet functionally ineffective, compensatory BDNF response in the hippocampus.
